mainTopic: The 'talking cow' and 'talking door' נזירות vows: רמי בר חמא's explanation, why the examples are repeated, and רבא's challenge and new attempts
overview: The עמוד opens by finishing an earlier discussion: the משנה had to teach that someone who pledges a barley מנחה brings one from wheat. Next comes a new משנה about odd vows, where a person says a cow or a door 'said' it is a נזיר. בית שמאי say he is a נזיר, בית הלל say he is not, and רבי יהודה limits בית שמאי's ruling. The גמרא asks how a cow can talk. רמי בר חמא explains that the man vowed to be a נזיר 'from its meat' if the cow stood up by itself, so each side follows its view from the dried-figs case. The גמרא asks why בית שמאי's view is repeated. רבא answers that a teacher often gives two or three examples, and the גמרא shows why the figs, meat and door cases are each needed. רבא then rejects רמי בר חמא's reading, because the משנה never says 'by itself.' His first replacement, that the man vowed the cow as a קרבן, fails because a door cannot be a קרבן. רבא begins a new explanation that continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Why the משנה needed to teach that one brings wheat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining what we would have wrongly thought without the משנה: a barley pledge works only if it matches an existing barley offering. The משנה teaches that he brings a wheat מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think: if the pledge can work as a barley offering like the מנחת סוטה, it becomes holy, and if not, nothing happens. So the משנה teaches us that he brings an offering made from wheat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is wrapping up an earlier discussion. It explains why the משנה about pledging a barley מנחה had to say that he brings one from wheat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Barley offerings exist only in special cases, like the מנחת סוטה. Without the משנה, we might say a barley pledge either matches such an offering or is worth nothing. The משנה teaches that the pledge still counts, and he fulfills it with a regular wheat מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: The barley offering brought by a woman suspected of being unfaithful
It becomes holy (it takes effect as an offering)
It teaches us (introduces the new lesson of a source)

steps.whatToRemember: Someone who pledges a barley מנחה still brings a regular wheat מנחה. The pledge is not thrown out.

phrases.english: or like the meal-offering of a סוטה,
it should become consecrated;
and if not, then not.
So it teaches us
that he brings from wheat.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּמַיְיתֵי מִן הַחִיטִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion that came before this section about the barley מנחה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains what the משנה's wording is needed for
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A barley pledge counts only if it matches a real barley offering. Otherwise it is void.

steps.title: The משנה: a cow or a door 'says' it is a נזיר
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה brings strange vows where a person says a cow or a door declared itself a נזיר. בית שמאי say he becomes a נזיר; בית הלל say he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone said, 'This cow said: I am a נזיר if I stand up,' or 'This door says: I am a נזיר if I am opened,' בית שמאי say he is a נזיר, and בית הלל say he is not a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It gives two odd vow statements and records a disagreement between בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording sounds as if the cow or the door is the one making the vow, which makes no sense. The argument is whether the person speaking becomes a נזיר. The גמרא will soon explain what the case really is.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks the start of a new משנה)
I am hereby a נזיר (feminine form)

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If one said: 'This cow said:
I am hereby a nazirite if I stand up';
or 'This door says:
I am hereby a nazirite if I am opened' —
Beit Shammai say: he is a nazirite;
and Beit Hillel say: he is not a nazirite.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר: ״אָמְרָה פָּרָה זוֹ הֲרֵינִי נְזִירָה אִם עוֹמֶדֶת אֲנִי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: he is a נזיר. בית הלל: he is not a נזיר.

steps.title: רבי יהודה limits בית שמאי's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says בית שמאי only meant a case where the man said, 'This cow is a קרבן to me if it stands.' That is a vow forbidding the cow, not נזירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: even when בית שמאי said the vow works, they said it only about someone who says, 'This cow is a קרבן to me if it stands up.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds his view to the משנה. He narrows what בית שמאי really meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהודה, בית שמאי never said such a person becomes a נזיר. They only said the cow becomes forbidden to him, the way a קרבן is forbidden. So the vow does take effect, but as a ban on the cow, not as נזירות.

keyTerms.meaning: Is to me like a קרבן (forbidden to me)
They only said (this limits a ruling)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה is not saying בית שמאי make him a נזיר. In his version, the vow only makes the cow forbidden to him.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
Even when Beit Shammai said it,
they said it only about one who says:
'This cow is hereby an offering to me
if it stands up.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף כְּשֶׁאָמְרוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי, לֹא אוֹמְרִים אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the meaning of בית שמאי's ruling in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי only meant that the cow becomes forbidden like a קרבן. They did not mean the man becomes a נזיר.

steps.title: Can a cow talk?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's wording: a cow does not speak, so what does 'this cow said' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and attacks the strange wording of the משנה. A cow cannot make a vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is phrased like a simple question, but it works as a challenge. Taken literally, the משנה's case is impossible, so the גמרא needs a sensible explanation of what the man actually said.

keyTerms.meaning: גמרא (marks the start of the discussion on the משנה)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Does a cow speak?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the משנה's first case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Animals cannot speak or make vows, so the case as written makes no sense.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא: the man vowed about the cow's meat
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא explains the case. A cow was lying down, and the man said, 'This cow thinks it won't stand. I am a נזיר from its meat if it gets up by itself,' and it got up. Each side follows its usual view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said: What case are we dealing with? A cow was lying in front of him, and he said, 'This cow thinks it will not stand. I am a נזיר from its meat if it stands up by itself.' It then stood up by itself. בית שמאי follow their usual view, and בית הלל follow their usual view.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא answers the challenge. He explains that the man, not the cow, made the vow. The words 'the cow said' describe what the cow 'thinks.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the vow makes sense: the man vowed to be a נזיר but tied it only to the cow's meat, which has nothing to do with נזירות. The argument depends on that odd mix, and each side follows a view it already holds elsewhere.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (introduces a specific setup)

phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama said:
With what are we dealing here?
Where a cow was lying down in front of him,
and he said: 'This cow thinks it will not stand;
I am hereby a nazirite from its flesh
if it stands up by itself.'
And it stood up by itself.
And Beit Shammai follow their approach,
and Beit Hillel follow their approach.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge 'Does a cow talk?'
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case (the man is the one vowing)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The cow itself seems to be making the vow.
steps.terutzMaskana: The man vowed to be a נזיר from the cow's meat if it stood up by itself.
steps.whyThisMatters: Once the case is clear, the argument turns out to be about a נזירות vow tied to something unrelated, which links it to an earlier argument.

steps.title: How each side follows its view on 'dried figs'
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי ruled that a vow to be a נזיר 'from dried figs' still makes a person a נזיר, so 'from its meat' makes him a נזיר too. בית הלל say he is not a נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say that one who vows to be a נזיר 'from dried figs and from fig cakes' is a נזיר. So here too, when he says 'from its meat,' he is a נזיר. And בית הלל say he is not a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out how each school is following its usual approach. It connects this case to the earlier argument about vowing נזירות from figs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Figs and beef have nothing to do with נזירות, which forbids grape products. בית שמאי hold the first words 'I am a נזיר' and ignore the added words. בית הלל hold that the vow does not make him a נזיר.

keyTerms.meaning: A pressed cake of dried figs
Here too (applies the same logic to a new case)

steps.whatToRemember: The cow case works the same way as the earlier fig case. בית שמאי say a נזירות vow tied to something unrelated still makes him a נזיר; בית הלל say it does not.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai, who say
that one who vows 'from dried figs and from fig cakes'
is a nazirite,
here too, when he says 'from its flesh,'
he is a nazirite.

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: לָא הָוֵי נָזִיר.
phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say: he is not a nazirite.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי דְּאָמְרִי ״מִן הַגְּרוֹגְרוֹת וּמִן הַדְּבֵילָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains 'each follows their approach' from the previous step.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The argument over the cow follows the fig argument. בית שמאי make him a נזיר, and בית הלל do not.

steps.title: Didn't בית שמאי already say this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we need this משנה at all, since בית שמאי already taught the same idea in the dried-figs case.
steps.simpleTranslation: But בית שמאי already said this rule once!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects to רמי בר חמא's explanation. If he is right, this משנה just repeats the earlier dried-figs ruling of בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רמי בר חמא, the cow case is just another 'I am a נזיר from X' vow. That is exactly the dried-figs case from the earlier משנה. So why would the משנה teach the same מחלוקת twice?

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that... (opens a challenge)

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אַמְרוּהָ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי חֲדָא זִימְנָא!
phrases.english: But didn't Beit Shammai already say it one time!
phrases.notes: He means the earlier משנה about being a נזיר 'from dried figs.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אַמְרוּהָ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי חֲדָא זִימְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the result of רמי בר חמא's explanation (steps 5-6) as making the משנה repetitive.
steps.kashyaTarget: רמי בר חמא's explanation of the cow case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the cow case is the same as the dried-figs case, the משנה is repeating itself for no reason.

steps.title: The תנא likes to give two or three examples
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that it is normal to teach the same idea through two or three cases. רבי חייא and רבי אושעיא did the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: two, three. And so רבי חייא taught two, three. And so רבי אושעיא said two, three.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends the repetition. Teaching the same principle with two or three examples is a normal teaching style.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Repeating an idea is not wasteful if each example adds something. רבא supports this with two other sages, רבי חייא and רבי אושעיא, who also taught this view of בית שמאי with several examples.

keyTerms.meaning: Two, three (several examples of one idea)

phrases.english: Rava said: two, three.
phrases.notes: Short for: the תנא teaches the same idea through two or three cases.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן תָּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא תַּרְתֵּי תְּלָת.
phrases.english: And so Rabbi Ḥiyya taught two, three.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא תַּרְתֵּי תְּלָת.
phrases.english: And so Rabbi Oshaya said two, three.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Teaching style: several examples of one principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One example should have been enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is normal to give two or three examples, and others did the same.

steps.title: Why we need both the figs case and the meat case
steps.stepSummary: Figs can be confused with grapes, and meat goes together with wine. Each case has its own reason, so we need both to learn that בית שמאי rule the same way in each.
steps.simpleTranslation: And both are needed. If it only said dried figs, I would think בית שמאי make him a נזיר only there, because figs get confused with grapes, but meat does not. If it only said meat, I would think בית שמאי say so only there, because meat and wine go together, but not figs. So the משנה teaches us both.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that each example adds something new. Each case has its own special reason that someone might think he meant wine or grapes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With figs, the link to נזירות is that figs look like grapes. With meat, the link is that people eat meat with wine. Since the reasons are different, one case cannot teach the other, so both are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: A pressed cake of dried figs
It teaches us (that this is not so)

phrases.english: And they are needed,
for if it were said only in this case of dried figs and fig cake:

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם הוּא דְּאָמְרִי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי הָוֵי נָזִיר,
phrases.english: it is there that Beit Shammai say he is a nazirite,
because they get confused with grapes.
But meat is not confused with grapes.
And if it were said only about meat:

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא הוּא דְּאָמְרִי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי הָוֵי נָזִיר
phrases.english: it is here that Beit Shammai say he is a nazirite,
because of meat and wine.
phrases.notes: Meat and wine are often eaten together, so he may have had wine in mind.

phrases.english: But dried figs and fig cake, no.
So it teaches us (both).

steps.triggerLanguage: וּצְרִיכִי, דְּאִי אִיתְּמַר בְּהָא גְּרוֹגְרוֹת וּדְבֵילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up רבא's answer by showing why each example is needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each case has its own reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בית שמאי might apply only to figs, or only to meat.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both cases are needed to show that בית שמאי rule the same way in each.

steps.title: Why we also need the door case
steps.stepSummary: Without the door case, we might think בית שמאי agree with בית הלל there. Without the figs and meat cases, we might think בית הלל agree with בית שמאי there. So all three cases are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If only these two cases were taught, I would say בית שמאי rule this way only here, but with a door they agree with בית הלל. If only the door were taught, I would say בית הלל rule this way only there, but in the other two cases they agree with בית שמאי. So it teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining why every example is needed. Now it adds the door case to the figs and meat cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A door has nothing to do with wine or grapes, so it is the weakest case for בית שמאי. Figs and meat are the strongest cases for בית שמאי, so they are the hardest cases for בית הלל. Teaching all of them shows that each side keeps its view even in the case that is hardest for it.

keyTerms.meaning: I would say (I might have thought)

steps.whatToRemember: The figs, meat and door cases all show the same מחלוקת. בית שמאי make him a נזיר in all of them, and בית הלל do not, even in the case that is hardest for each side.

phrases.english: And if only these two were said:
phrases.notes: These two are the figs case and the meat case.

phrases.english: it is in these that Beit Shammai say so,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל דֶּלֶת אֵימָא מוֹדוּ לְהוּ לְבֵית הִלֵּל.
phrases.english: but with a door, I would say they agree with Beit Hillel.
And if it taught only the door:
it is in this case that Beit Hillel say so,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּהָךְ תַּרְתֵּי אֵימָא מוֹדוּ לְהוּ לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי,
phrases.english: but in those two, I would say they agree with Beit Shammai.
So it teaches us that this is not so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the explanation of why each case is needed, now adding the door case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each case is the hardest test for one side
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each side might give in on the case that is hardest for its own view.
steps.terutzMaskana: Neither side gives in. The מחלוקת holds in all three cases.

steps.title: The משנה never says 'by itself'
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רמי בר חמא: the משנה only says 'if it stands.' It never says 'if it stands by itself.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Does the משנה teach 'if it stood by itself'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises a second problem with רמי בר חמא's explanation. This time the problem is the wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רמי בר חמא's case depends on the cow standing up by itself. The משנה only says 'if it stands.' So רבא argues that רמי בר חמא is adding a detail the משנה does not have.

keyTerms.meaning: Does it teach...? (pointing out missing wording)

phrases.english: Rava said:
Does it teach: 'If it stood by itself'?
phrases.notes: The משנה just says 'if it stands.' The words 'by itself' came from רמי בר חמא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מִי קָתָנֵי ״אִם עָמְדָה מֵאֵלֶיהָ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the repetition question is settled, רבא attacks רמי בר חמא's explanation from a new angle.
steps.kashyaTarget: רמי בר חמא's detail that the cow stood up by itself
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's wording does not include 'by itself,' so his case does not fit the text.

steps.title: רבא's first attempt: he vowed the cow as a קרבן
steps.stepSummary: רבא suggests a different case. A cow was lying in front of the man, and he said, 'It is upon me as a קרבן.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: The case is where a cow was lying in front of him, and he said, 'It is upon me as a קרבן.'
steps.whatsHappening: Since רמי בר חמא's reading does not fit, רבא gives his own explanation of the cow case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading, the man takes on the cow as a נזיר's קרבן. בית שמאי would treat that as taking on נזירות. The new reading does not need the cow to stand 'by itself.'

keyTerms.meaning: It is upon me (wording of a vow)
An offering brought in the בית המקדש

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
For example, where a cow was lying in front of him,
and he said: 'It is upon me as an offering.'
phrases.notes: He is taking the cow on as a נזיר's offering, and so taking on נזירות.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: כְּגוֹן שֶׁהָיְתָה פָּרָה רְבוּצָה לְפָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רמי בר חמא's case after רבא's wording challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case needs a cow that stood up by itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is a vow that takes on the cow as a קרבן.

steps.title: A door cannot be a קרבן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבא's first attempt. A cow can be a קרבן, but the משנה also has a door case, and a door cannot be a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for a cow, since a cow can be a קרבן. But can a door be a קרבן?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down רבא's new reading by checking it against the door case in the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Any explanation has to work for both the cow and the door. A door can never be brought as an offering. So the 'קרבן' reading cannot explain the door case.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense for... (sets up a contrast)

phrases.english: It makes sense for a cow; it can be an offering.
But a door, can it be an offering?!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא פָּרָה בַּת קׇרְבָּן הִיא, אֶלָּא דֶּלֶת בַּת קׇרְבָּן הִיא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The explanation must also fit the door case, and a door cannot be a קרבן.

steps.title: רבא starts a new explanation
steps.stepSummary: רבא tries again, starting with the same picture: a cow was lying in front of the man. His explanation continues in the next lines.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: The case is where a cow was lying in front of him...
steps.whatsHappening: This line is setting up רבא's next try. He starts describing the case, and the rest of his explanation comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא keeps the same starting picture of a cow lying in front of the man. He drops the 'קרבן' idea, since it failed for the door. The rest of his new case has not been given yet.

keyTerms.meaning: For example, the case is like...

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
For example, where a cow was lying in front of him,
